findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an engineer opens a story on a fresh teammate clone after a part merged more than six weeks ago, with its review history stored in its pull request.
Done when: On the board, a story with merged parts lists each part's review rounds under the part's plain title, from its full history, and counts them in the story's review rounds figure.
The item read is not complete in this case: src/forge/board.py:218 clears the expired set for the untrimmed view, so the older-PR body lookup at src/forge/board.py:696-703 is skipped. The ordinary PR search covers only six full weeks (src/forge/board_facts.py:216-220). Without local events or an earlier backfill cache, the part has an empty rounds list, so both the drawer and full page omit its reviews and show a count that is too low.
findings.title: Not done: Show merged parts' review rounds from published full history

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a story has one reviewed, merged part and another part whose first worker turn is still being built.
The new total counts every entry in each child's rounds array as a review. However, src/forge/time_records.py:200-225 creates an attempt for a worker turn even when it has no review result or review timing, and lines 325-393 put that attempt in rounds. The story therefore lists the unreviewed work as a review round and reports two reviews when only one occurred.
findings.title: The story count includes work that has not been reviewed

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a teammate reads a part's history from its pull request, or a story has its own review rounds alongside its parts' rounds.
The sole proof puts every part's review events in the board machine's local log and gives the story an empty rounds list. It would still pass if older PR-only rounds were omitted, the story's own rounds were ignored, or an unreviewed worker turn were counted. It also calls Board.openDrawer directly at line 43 and selects the count through the .figures div structure at line 53, so a behaviour-preserving UI refactor can break the test. Exercise the story through the board and assert the displayed facts for those cases.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_board_story_rounds_from_parts.py::test_1_a_story_whose_parts_merged_lists_their_rounds_and_counts_them

why: A story whose parts have merged says "No review rounds yet" and shows an unknown review round count, even though its review rounds sit on its parts.
